svg.title: Quick reference tabs for cognitive science. Choosing a stats test: 2 groups, independent t test or Mann Whitney if non normal; same people in 2 conditions, paired t test or Wilcoxon signed rank; 3 or more groups, one way ANOVA or Kruskal Wallis; trials nested in participants, linear mixed model (lmer) with random effects; binary outcome, logistic mixed model (glmer, binomial); many channels by time points, cluster based permutation tests. EEG frequency bands: delta 0.5 to 4 Hz deep sleep; theta 4 to 8 Hz memory encoding and cognitive control; alpha 8 to 13 Hz relaxed wakefulness and inhibition; beta 13 to 30 Hz active thinking and motor control; gamma 30 to 100 Hz feature binding and perception. ERP components by latency: ERN about 50 to 100 ms after an error, P1 about 100 ms, N1 100 to 200 ms, N170 about 170 ms for faces, MMN 150 to 250 ms auditory deviance, P300 300 to 600 ms context updating, N400 about 400 ms semantic violations, LPP 400 to 1000+ ms emotional salience. lme4 mixed model syntax: random intercept (1 | g), intercept and slope (1 + x | g), crossed effects (1 | a) + (1 | b). Three pass reading: pass 1, 5 minutes, title, abstract, figures, conclusion; pass 2, 30 minutes, intro and methods; pass 3, deep, results in detail and limitations. Also a brain regions tab.

div.h3: Reading a paper in three passes

div.div: 1 · 5 minTitle, abstract, figures, conclusion. Worth it?
2 · 30 minIntro and methods: question, sample, design, analysis.
3 · deepResults in detail. Could you rerun it? Limitations?
Plus a brain regions tab: prefrontal cortex to cerebellum, with key functions.
